lines: These files are public by design, so what gitleaks matches in them is not reported:
appinfo/signature.json, the integrity signature: 333 matches in 2 commits.

In these generated files gitleaks matches only rules that take any string of high entropy, which hashes and minified names are as well, or the curl lines a page of built documentation copies from its source, so the matches are not reported as secrets:
js/vendor/forge.0.6.9.min.js, a minified file: 4 matches in what ships, 6 matches in 1 commit (generic-api-key).
js/passman.min.js, a minified file: 6 matches in 2 commits (generic-api-key).
A key a build takes from the environment ends up in such a file too: where one of them has no reason to carry a key, look at it.

These files are test data, the report of a test run or example code, whose keys and tokens are made up or serve a test, so the matches are not reported as secrets. Those of a private key or a GitHub token are:
tests/Unit/Db/CredentialRevisionTest.php, test data: 2 matches in 1 commit (generic-api-key).
tests/db/dumps/oc_passman_revisions.xml, test data: 1 match in 1 commit (generic-api-key).
tests/Unit/Db/CredentialTest.php, test data: 1 match in 1 commit (generic-api-key).
tests/Unit/Db/ShareRequestTest.php, test data: 1 match in 1 commit (generic-api-key).
tests/Unit/Db/SharingACLTest.php, test data: 1 match in 1 commit (generic-api-key).
tests/unit/lib/Db/CredentialTest.php, test data: 1 match in 1 commit (generic-api-key).
tests/unit/lib/Db/ShareRequestTest.php, test data: 1 match in 1 commit (generic-api-key).
tests/unit/lib/Db/SharingACLTest.php, test data: 1 match in 1 commit (generic-api-key).
A token a test run used against a real server stays valid until it is revoked: where one of these files holds one, revoke it.
